tool.name: TIDDIT SV
tool.description: call structural variants from paired-end WGS alignments
tool.command:
@LINK_BAM@
#if str($reference_source.ref_selector) == 'cached': ln -s '${reference_source.ref.fields.path}' reference.fa && ln -s '${reference_source.ref.fields.path}.fai' reference.fa.fai && #elif $reference_source.ref.is_of_type('fasta.gz'): ## TIDDIT and bwa index want a plain FASTA they can index in place gunzip -c '${reference_source.ref}' > reference.fa && #else: ln -s '${reference_source.ref}' reference.fa && #end if
#if str($assembly.mode) == 'build_index': bwa index reference.fa && #end if
python '$check_header' './${sample_name}.bam' &&
tiddit --sv --bam './${sample_name}.bam' --ref reference.fa -o tiddit --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} #if str($assembly.mode) == 'skip': --skip_assembly #end if -q $calling.min_mapq -p $calling.min_pairs -r $calling.min_split_reads -z $calling.min_size -n $calling.ploidy --min_contig $calling.min_contig #if str($calling.insert_size): -i $calling.insert_size #end if #if str($calling.coverage): -c $calling.coverage #end if --p_ratio $filtering.p_ratio --r_ratio $filtering.r_ratio --max_coverage $filtering.max_coverage
## TIDDIT reports its own errors on stdout and still exits 0. && if [ ! -s tiddit.vcf ]; then echo 'TIDDIT did not produce a VCF; see the tool standard output for the reason.' >&2; exit 1; fi

configfiles.configfile:
import sys
import pysam
header = pysam.AlignmentFile(sys.argv[1], check_sq=False).header.to_dict() samples = sorted(set(rg["SM"] for rg in header.get("RG", []) if "SM" in rg)) if len(samples) > 1: sys.exit( "The BAM file has read groups for %d samples. TIDDIT would call them as one sample; " "give it one sample per BAM file." % len(samples) ) contigs = [sq["SN"] for sq in header.get("SQ", [])] if any("/" in name for name in samples + contigs): sys.exit("TIDDIT cannot use sample or contig names that contain a slash; rename them in the BAM header first.")

param.help: Minimum number of supporting split reads needed to call a variant.

param.label: Minimum variant size (bp)

param.label: Maximum insert size of normal pairs (bp)
param.help: Pairs on the same chromosome further apart than this are SV candidates. Leave empty to use the 99.9th percentile of the observed insert size.

tool.help:
## What it does
[TIDDIT](https://github.com/SciLifeLab/TIDDIT) calls structural variants (deletions, duplications, inversions, insertions and translocations) from short-read whole-genome sequencing data. It combines discordant read pairs, split reads and read depth, and can refine breakpoints by local assembly of soft-clipped reads.
## Inputs
- A coordinate-sorted BAM file of paired-end (or mate-pair) reads. - The reference genome the reads were aligned to, either a built-in genome or a FASTA dataset from your history.
If the BAM file has a read group with a sample (`SM`) tag, that name is used as the sample column of the VCF. Otherwise the dataset name is used, with a trailing `.bam` removed and any character other than letters, digits, `_` and `-` replaced by `_`.
## Local assembly
By default the tool runs TIDDIT with `--skip_assembly`. This is faster and does not need a BWA index of the reference, at the cost of somewhat less precise breakpoints. Choosing *Run local assembly* builds a BWA index of the reference inside the job and lets TIDDIT assemble soft-clipped reads. Indexing is quick for small genomes, but for a human-sized genome it takes about an hour and several GB of memory, on every run.
## Small genomes
TIDDIT skips contigs shorter than 10 kb by default. Lower *Minimum contig length* if your genome has small chromosomes or plasmids you want called.
## Outputs
- **VCF**: the structural variant calls. Calls failing TIDDIT's filters are kept and marked in the `FILTER` column. - **Ploidy table**: per-chromosome estimated ploidy and mean coverage.
